purpose: C02's second source had no declaration, so the acquisition gate refused every proxy by name. This records what the new declaration produces, and the refresh invariant it moved.

the_planner_declares: each annual accession's primary and index
why_a_separate_module.it_does_not_declare: the annual meeting proxy, or the Part III amendment where a company puts its governance information there
why_a_separate_module.consequence_before: HISTORICAL_URL_IS_NOT_A_DECLARED_DEPENDENCY for every C02 proxy, so no allowance could unblock those positions
why_a_separate_module.why_not_extend_the_planner: plan_historical_sources is a NEW_RULE_FILE of issue_47_v1; editing it moves the closure the last 374 frozen Runs were produced under
why_a_separate_module.how_the_rows_are_derived: by asking prepare_historical_business_text_input which filing that period's C02 would read, not by writing the proxy rule a second time - the same discipline the event declaration uses with _event_sources

marriott_measured.limitations: periods whose own annual primary is not saved declare nothing and carry a named limitation, rather than declaring zero

the_builder_refused.what_it_means: the two-phase design working: the candidate was never installed, so nothing named itself valid on bytes that had not passed
the_builder_refused.assertion: 115 != 116 : a refresh must not change what the frame declares

what_the_growth_actually_was.method: set difference by source_url over the chain's real before and after states
what_the_growth_actually_was.reading: the refresh unblocked JPMorgan's FY2025 period selection, so the declaration could name that period's proxy for the first time. FY2024 stays blocked because its shards were never saved and a derived index does not invent them.
what_the_growth_actually_was.so_the_declaration_is: a lower bound that grows as blockers clear - the same shape already recorded for the event declaration

why_the_equality_was_replaced.too_strict: it forbade explained growth together with the real fault
why_the_equality_was_replaced.too_loose: a swap - one row out, one row in - leaves the count untouched
replacement: test_the_refresh_drops_nothing_it_was_declaring: set difference must be empty, and the rows that carried the conflict must still be declared
test_anything_the_refresh_adds_is_a_period_it_unblocked: every added row must serve a period present in before's governance limitations and absent from after's, and some period must still be blocked
why_the_equality_was_replaced.deliberately_not_asserted: that an added row needs no fetch. This one is already saved, but a period that unblocks may name a proxy that is not, and that would be correct.

fault_injections.what_it_simulates: a chain that 'clears' the conflict by no longer declaring the shards that carried it - the fault the count equality was written against
a row that appears with nothing about the refresh accounting for it
the chain proving nothing, which the case must say rather than pass vacuously

fault_injections.first_version_was_broken: it dropped one and added one on top of a chain that already goes 115 -> 116, so the count equality would have failed anyway - for the wrong reason. An injection that cannot reach the point under test is not evidence.
fault_injections.second_version: drop two, add one, so the count lands exactly on before

a_second_shape_named_here.what: C02's source gap surfaces as a failed position, not a WITHHELD Run
a_second_shape_named_here.why: C02's second source is needed to prepare the Run's input. C04's missing index is needed to resolve the metric, so its Run exists and the result is WITHHELD. Manufacturing a Run here would mean declaring an input that does not exist.
a_second_shape_named_here.what_is_owed: the frame must read this as a source gap, not as an unexplained attempt failure
